subtopics.title: Temperature, Pressure and Wind — the Chain

questions.question: The correct causal chain at the surface is:
options: Wind creates pressure differences, which then change the temperature
Warm air rises so surface pressure falls and a low forms; cold air sinks so surface pressure rises and a high forms; wind then flows from high to low
High pressure always forms over warm surfaces
Pressure is unrelated to temperature

questions.question: On a weather chart, isobars packed tightly together indicate:
options: A steep pressure gradient and strong wind
Light, calm conditions
Heavy rainfall
A temperature inversion

questions.question: The weather pairing that settles most questions in this topic is:
options: Lows bring clear skies; highs bring storms
Both lows and highs bring rain in summer only
In a low, air rises, cools and condenses, giving cloud and rain; in a high, air subsides, warms and dries, giving clear settled weather
Pressure cells have no effect on weather

questions.question: A wind arriving from the south-west is named and given a bearing as:
options: A north-easterly at 045 degrees, since winds are named for their destination
A south-westerly at 135 degrees
A westerly at 270 degrees
A south-westerly at 225 degrees, since winds are named for the direction they come from and each of the 16 compass points spans 22,5 degrees

questions.question: The doldrums of the equatorial low are calm because:
options: Surface winds converge there and the air escapes upward, leaving horizontal winds weak and fitful
No radiation reaches the equator
The Coriolis force is strongest at the equator
Cold sinking air suppresses all motion

questions.question: The world's great deserts cluster near 30 degrees north and south because:
options: Those latitudes receive the least insolation
Air that rose at the equator subsides there, warming and drying as it descends under the subtropical highs
Ocean currents cannot reach those latitudes
The polar front passes overhead twice a year

questions.question: The three semi-permanent anticyclones that dominate southern Africa's weather are:
options: The Azores High, the Siberian High and the polar high
Three travelling lows over the interior
The South Atlantic High, the South Indian High and the continental high over the plateau
The equatorial low, the polar front and the jet stream

questions.question: The south-western Cape receives its rain in winter because:
options: Summer heating evaporates all its moisture
The ITCZ crosses the Cape each June
Sea temperatures peak in winter
The pressure belts shift about five degrees north in June, letting the westerlies and their cold fronts sweep over the south-western corner of the country

subtopics.title: The Tri-cellular Circulation and the Forces That Bend It

questions.question: The Hadley cell is the strongest of the three cells because:
options: It is driven directly by equatorial heating — rising air at the equator, subsidence at 30 degrees, trade winds returning along the surface
It is spun by the two cells beside it
It contains no vertical motion
It operates only in summer

questions.question: The Ferrel cell between 30 and 60 degrees is described as indirect because:
options: It flows in the same direction as the trade winds
It is not powered by its own heating but is dragged around by the Hadley and polar cells on either side
It exists only over the oceans
It reverses direction each season

questions.question: The Coriolis force in the Southern Hemisphere:
options: Deflects moving air to the right and speeds it up
Acts only on ocean currents
Deflects moving air to the left, is zero at the equator and greatest at the poles, and changes direction but never speed
Pushes all air toward the equator

questions.question: Geostrophic flow occurs above about one kilometre because:
options: The pressure gradient force disappears at height
The air is too thin to move
Jet streams block all other winds
Friction falls away, the pressure gradient and Coriolis forces balance exactly, and the wind blows parallel to straight isobars

subtopics.title: Air Masses, Berg Winds and Monsoons

questions.question: An air mass takes its temperature and moisture character from:
options: The source region where it stagnated, modifying gradually as it travels
The jet stream above it
The season in which it is named
The isobars it crosses

questions.question: Gqeberha's cool late-afternoon onshore wind in summer exists because:
options: The ocean heats faster than the land by day
Daytime heating lowers pressure over the land faster than over the sea, drawing a cool sea breeze onshore
The berg wind reverses each afternoon
The polar front arrives each afternoon

questions.question: Air leaves the plateau rim at 1 500 metres at 14 degrees Celsius and descends to sea level as a berg wind. Using the dry adiabatic lapse rate of 1 degree per 100 metres, its arrival temperature is:
options: 15 degrees Celsius
44 degrees Celsius
29 degrees Celsius, because 1 500 divided by 100 gives 15 degrees of warming added to 14
14 degrees Celsius, because descending air keeps its temperature

questions.question: A monsoon is best described as:
options: A tropical cyclone that returns each year
A berg wind operating over the ocean
A permanent trade wind
A seasonal reversal of wind driven by the land heating faster than the sea in summer and cooling faster in winter — a sea breeze at continental scale

subtopics.title: Smoke, Freezers and the Bicycle Pump

questions.question: Campfire smoke always climbing and freezer air always spilling downward together demonstrate that:
options: Warm air rises to make surface lows while cold dense air sinks to make surface highs
Smoke is lighter than all air and cold air is heavier than all smoke
Fires create high pressure and freezers create low pressure
Vertical motion has no link to pressure

questions.question: In the packed-hall picture of wind, tightly squeezed isobars correspond to:
options: A hall with nobody in it
A desperate crush emptying through a nearby doorway — a big pressure difference over a short distance, so a strong wind
Doors that are locked shut
People moving from the empty corridor into the hall

questions.question: The bicycle pump barrel warming in your hand explains why:
options: Lows bring thunderstorms
Wind blows parallel to isobars
Air sinking in a high is compressed and warmed, drying it out and giving clear, cloudless weather
The trade winds blow from the south-east

questions.question: In the escalator picture, the ring of deserts at 30 degrees south exists because:
options: Air from the equatorial loop steps off downward there, and descending air warms and dries
The escalators carry moisture away from the equator
No sunlight reaches 30 degrees
The polar loop delivers frozen air there

questions.question: The middle loop between 30 and 60 degrees is the freeloader because:
options: It carries no wind at all
It has no heat engine of its own and is dragged around by the loops on either side, its surface wind being the westerlies
It runs backwards in winter
It only operates over land

questions.question: The jet streams are found:
options: Along the surface at the equator
Inside the subtropical highs
Near the top of the troposphere at the boundaries between cells, as narrow cores of west-to-east wind passing 200 kilometres per hour
Below the friction layer

questions.question: The five-degree seasonal slide of the belts means that South Africa:
options: Receives rain everywhere in every season
Has no rainfall pattern at all
Receives frontal rain inland in summer
Gets winter frontal rain in the south-western corner when the belts shift north, and summer thunderstorm rain inland when the belts shift south

questions.question: The chalk line drawn dead straight across a spinning lazy Susan comes out curved because:
options: The surface rotated underneath the straight-moving chalk — the same reason moving air appears deflected on the rotating earth
The chalk was pushed sideways by the tray
Chalk cannot draw straight lines on plastic
The tray tilted while spinning

questions.question: Standing with your back to the wind in South Africa, Buys Ballot's Law places:
options: High pressure on your right
Low pressure on your right, from which it follows that our lows spin clockwise and our highs anticlockwise
Low pressure directly behind you
The wind at your left shoulder always

questions.question: The berg wind arrives at the coast scorching and dry because:
options: It picks up heat from the warm ocean
It starts as humid tropical air
Falling from the plateau it is compressed and warms about 1 degree per 100 metres while gaining no moisture, so its relative humidity collapses
It blows only at midday in summer

questions.question: Calling the monsoon a sea breeze that swapped its wristwatch for a calendar means:
options: Monsoons happen only in the afternoon
Monsoons and sea breezes both blow from land to sea
The monsoon is driven by ocean currents rather than pressure
The same land-sea heating contrast that reverses a coastal breeze daily reverses the monsoon seasonally, flooding India with moist ocean air in summer and draining dry air seaward in winter
